critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/setup-walk/build.sh — sed -E regex `(/setup_walk\.compiled\.js)(\?v=[a-f0-9]+)?` correctly idempotent: handles BOTH first-run (no ?v= yet) and rebuild cases. Uses md5sum first 10 chars (~40 bits, sufficient collision resistance for a cache-bust token).

/app/frontend/src/dashboard/build.sh — same pattern, also fixed earlier mktemp leak by using deterministic /tmp/red5_dashboard_concat.jsx so source-map inline hash is stable; this is what makes the build deterministic (same input → same hash twice in a row).
Both build scripts also rewrite the HTML comment line that mentions the bundle filename — verified harmless because the regex matches BOTH the <script src> AND the comment, keeping them in sync.
Cache-bust uses ?v=<hash> as a query string only (no filename change) — this is the standard, safe approach (CDN respects URL, browser cache key includes query string, no orphaned files left over).

No code regressions: Psy Chart Setting full-page editor still shows all controls (Display Mode block, Givoni toggle, RH preset dropdown with 10 options, RH lo/hi sliders, T-axis sliders, Save & return button). rca of the issue: User saw stale setup.html bundle because the browser had cached an old /setup_walk.compiled.js from a prior visit (filename never changed across builds). Fix: both build.sh scripts now compute md5sum first-10-chars of the compiled bundle and `sed -E` inject ?v=<HASH> into the script src in setup.html / dashboard.html. Result: every rebuild changes the URL → cache key invalidated → browser refetches. Verified the HTML served to clients carries the correct ?v= hash, the live DOM <script> src matches, the Display Mode block renders, and the build is deterministic (same source → same hash on repeated runs).
